name: Introduction
problem:
The unit circle provides a convenient way to represent the sine and cosine of special angles in each quadrant. 

We first recall the following:

- The ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250054/assets/fcc5df999e3b49fae1685ee0ab5bd03709804e1dd49f2ee722c4269eb0f5506d.svg)-coordinate of any point on the unit circle equals the *cosine* of the corresponding central angle, and

- the ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250054/assets/1d9b846cface9f9348e4081a0dd87dd254bf26663c12aa0d1a15aa24d2393261.svg)-coordinate equals the *sine* of the corresponding central angle.

Let's use the unit circle to list the special values of sine and cosine, starting with the first quadrant. First, we mark off the special angles in this quadrant.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250054/assets/3a0c6eb5bc286272ef67aee5ef0fa625a6f4e44635413ca43060efc9082b1848.png)

Now, let's write down each point's ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250054/assets/fcc5df999e3b49fae1685ee0ab5bd03709804e1dd49f2ee722c4269eb0f5506d.svg)- and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250054/assets/1d9b846cface9f9348e4081a0dd87dd254bf26663c12aa0d1a15aa24d2393261.svg)-coordinates, corresponding to the cosine and sine of each point's central angle. In addition, we'll highlight the ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250054/assets/1d9b846cface9f9348e4081a0dd87dd254bf26663c12aa0d1a15aa24d2393261.svg)-coordinate at each point.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250054/assets/6bb6bb7cc95a17c605056e1e1e1ae27bc8cf2f124e419c5e6b9810a72b950508.png)

Before we move on, observe that if we rotate counterclockwise from the positive ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250054/assets/fcc5df999e3b49fae1685ee0ab5bd03709804e1dd49f2ee722c4269eb0f5506d.svg)-axis, we see that the ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250054/assets/1d9b846cface9f9348e4081a0dd87dd254bf26663c12aa0d1a15aa24d2393261.svg)-coordinates at the special angles are given by the following sequence:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250054/assets/ef3998f9651e37dba31e1597a503577243def17e903dbeb5322ab434a4815b3c.svg) 

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250054/assets/ae75322c270db13d7ee5ba6079b236b9a18d463f74cc3e5ee70b6fe113d224e3.png)

There is a similar pattern for the ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250054/assets/fcc5df999e3b49fae1685ee0ab5bd03709804e1dd49f2ee722c4269eb0f5506d.svg)-coordinates (corresponding to the cosine of the central angle). The only difference is that now we go in reverse, from ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250054/assets/2614c435bff188ded3027f2a8f1ea011b37b41a1d62d2ff4bae181ce9107b5c2.svg) to ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250054/assets/f12b2ec86446e22fc9d1c982c156c7d089a97fecca1670f416ecfd63cf5899d3.svg) as shown below
